question: What is the primary purpose of research dissemination in nursing?

options.B: To ensure discoveries inform clinical practice and health policy
options.C: To restrict patient access to medical information
options.D: To increase the workload of hospital administrators

explanation: Dissemination ensures that valuable scientific discoveries actively inform clinical practice, health policy, and patient care outcomes rather than remaining hidden. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T2#GNS224_U4_T2_h1)

question: Why do different stakeholders require tailored dissemination approaches?

options.A: Because all stakeholders have the exact same educational background
options.B: To ensure the research achieves its intended impact on various groups
options.C: To make the research process as complicated as possible
options.D: Because patients never read research findings

explanation: Tailoring approaches to groups like nurses, policymakers, and the public increases the likelihood that research will achieve its intended impact. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T2#GNS224_U4_T2_h1)

question: What is the primary function of peer reviewers in academic publishing?

options.A: To rewrite the entire manuscript for the author
options.B: To rigorously evaluate methodology, ethics, and academic integrity
options.C: To charge high subscription fees for the journal
options.D: To translate the article into multiple local languages

explanation: Peer reviewers independently evaluate the work to validate methodology, ensure ethical compliance, and maintain high standards before publication. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T2#GNS224_U4_T2_h2)

question: What is a major advantage of open-access academic journals?

options.A: They completely eliminate the need for peer review
options.B: They allow free global access, expanding readership and citations
options.C: They guarantee immediate acceptance of any submitted manuscript
options.D: They restrict findings only to local hospital staff

explanation: Open-access formats allow free global access to articles, thereby expanding readership and citation rates significantly. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T2#GNS224_U4_T2_h2)

question: What are the two primary formats for presenting research at scientific conferences?

options.B: Oral podium presentations and visual poster displays
options.C: Social media threads and textbook chapters

explanation: Research at scientific conferences is typically presented either through oral podium presentations or visual poster displays. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T2#GNS224_U4_T2_h3)

question: Why is the networking aspect of scientific symposia particularly valuable for nursing students?

options.A: It allows them to build mentorship relationships and find collaborative partners
options.B: It replaces the need for formal clinical practice hours
options.C: It guarantees automatic publication in high-impact journals
options.D: It eliminates all challenges related to research funding

explanation: Face-to-face networking helps attendees build valuable mentorship relationships and exchange innovative ideas with experts. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T2#GNS224_U4_T2_h3)

question: What is the primary focus of professional workshops and seminars in research dissemination?

options.A: Translating evidence into actionable clinical skills and hands-on learning
options.B: Passing laws in the national legislature
options.C: Broadcasting entertainment to the general public

explanation: Workshops focus heavily on translating evidence into actionable clinical skills and practical application for frontline staff. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T2#GNS224_U4_T2_h4)

question: Why are workshops particularly effective for frontline nurses?

options.A: They allow nurses to practice operational steps needed for better patient care
options.B: They require no active participation or discussion
options.C: They replace the need for patient assessments
options.D: They focus exclusively on financial accounting

explanation: Workshops allow nurses to learn operational steps and practice techniques to integrate findings into daily routines. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T2#GNS224_U4_T2_h4)

question: What is the main purpose of a policy brief in research dissemination?

options.A: To publish raw, unanalyzed statistical data for peer review
options.B: To condense key findings and recommendations into a concise format for decision-makers
options.C: To entertain the general public with health stories
options.D: To serve as a textbook for nursing student examinations

explanation: Policy briefs condense key findings, impacts, and recommendations into concise documents that decision-makers can easily digest and act upon. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T2#GNS224_U4_T2_h5)

question: Why do policymakers benefit from stakeholder reports instead of full research papers?

options.A: Policy makers lack time to read dense academic manuscripts filled with jargon
options.B: Policy makers only read fiction books
options.C: Full research papers are illegal for politicians to look at
options.D: Stakeholder reports contain no scientific data

explanation: Decision-makers rarely have time for lengthy, dense academic manuscripts, so concise reports highlight urgent issues and proposed solutions effectively. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T2#GNS224_U4_T2_h5)

question: What is a primary advantage of using public forums for research dissemination?

options.A: They allow researchers to communicate findings directly to the affected population in accessible ways
options.B: They restrict participation only to university professors
options.C: They eliminate the need for ethical research approval
options.D: They focus exclusively on complex statistical formulas

explanation: Public forums allow researchers to communicate study outcomes and health strategies directly to everyday citizens in accessible, culturally sensitive ways. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T2#GNS224_U4_T2_h6)

question: Why is community engagement especially important in the Nigerian healthcare context?

options.A: Because cultural beliefs and community structures heavily influence health behaviors
options.B: Because Nigerians refuse to visit modern hospitals
options.C: Because community forums replace all other forms of clinical research
options.D: Because it is required by international copyright law

explanation: Local structures and cultural beliefs heavily influence health behaviors in Nigeria, making community engagement and culturally relevant communication crucial. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T2#GNS224_U4_T2_h6)

question: What do altmetrics measure regarding research findings?

options.A: The physical weight of printed academic journals
options.B: How widely research is discussed and shared online across digital platforms
options.C: The exact cost of conducting a clinical trial
options.D: The number of patients admitted to a hospital ward

explanation: Altmetrics measure how widely research is discussed online, providing a picture of public and professional engagement beyond traditional citations. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T2#GNS224_U4_T2_h7)

question: What is an important caution for nurses when using social media for research dissemination?

options.A: They must avoid sharing any information online
options.B: They must protect patient confidentiality and verify source credibility
options.C: They are required to pay high subscription fees to post tweets
options.D: They should only post research written in ancient languages

explanation: Nurses must exercise professional judgment, protect patient confidentiality, and verify source credibility to avoid spreading misinformation online. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T2#GNS224_U4_T2_h7)

question: What is the primary factor that should guide a researcher's choice of a dissemination channel?

options.A: The personal preference of the printer manufacturer
options.B: The target audience and how they prefer to consume information
options.C: The alphabetical order of the available dissemination platforms
options.D: The total number of pages in the research draft

explanation: Choosing a channel is a strategic decision that depends heavily on who needs to know the information and how that audience prefers to consume it. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T2#GNS224_U4_T2_h8)

question: If a researcher wants to change national healthcare policy, why might a journal article alone be insufficient?

options.A: Policymakers rarely read academic journals, so policy briefs and stakeholder meetings are also needed
options.B: Journal articles are illegal for politicians to read
options.C: Policy changes can only be made through social media tweets
options.D: Journal articles never contain scientific data

explanation: Policymakers need concise, actionable information, so journal articles must be paired with policy briefs and stakeholder meetings to achieve policy changes. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T2#GNS224_U4_T2_h8)
